items.title: Experiment: x402
items.body:
This PR is a little research experiment to figure out how hard it is to include x402 payments for sharing keys in indexd.
The goal would be to support configuring arbitrary facilitators instead of locking users into using a specific third party service. 

It should allow users to attach a price to a sharing key that has to be paid once to unlock it and make it usable. Payment is handled by a middleware that the 4 sharing endpoints are wrapped it that currently require a sharing key for authentication.

Next steps involve deploying an indexer on the testnet, creating a branch with support for this to the go sdk and then see if this works with testnet USDC.

The client purposefully doesn't handle any payments. It will let the caller check whether payment is required and the required price but the payment has to be created outside the client library and then passed to it.

Syncs `main` with `x402-foundation/x402` (upstream), which it has not tracked since **June 17, 2026**.

**200 commits, 2,221 files.**

### Why this is safe

- This fork's `main` is a **strict ancestor** of upstream `main` 鈥?it carries **zero unique commits**. Nothing here is overwritten or lost.
- All **200/200 commits are signature-verified**.
- The branch head is byte-identical to upstream `e398a9e5`.

| path | files |
|---|---|
| `typescript/site` | 539 |
| `typescript/packages` | 491 |
| `python/x402` | 220 |
| `e2e/servers` | 187 |
| `go/mechanisms` | 155 |

Includes 27 release/version commits across the npm, Go, and PyPI packages.

### Merge note

This is a fork-sync, so a **fast-forward** would be ideal 鈥?it keeps `main` identical to upstream and leaves future syncs trivial. The org ruleset on the default branch permits only `squash` and `rebase`, both of which rewrite these 200 commits into new SHAs and permanently diverge this fork's history from upstream. # Closes

standard primitives as Concerto models (first of the agentic-commerce family).

### Changes
- Adds `org.accordproject.protocol.x402@0.2.0` (`src/protocol/x402@0.2.0.cto`) 鈥?a
  Concerto model of the [x402](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402)
  internet-native payments protocol, spec v2 (source snapshot pinned in the file
  header): `PaymentRequired` / `PaymentRequirements`, `PaymentPayload` with the
  exact/EVM (EIP-3009) and exact/SVM scheme payloads, facilitator `/verify` and
  `/settle` responses, `/supported`, the HTTP header transport binding
  (`PAYMENT-REQUIRED` / `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` / `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`), the discovery
  (Bazaar) types, and the standard error-code enum.
- Demonstrates `org.accordproject.money@1.0.0.PreciseAmount` in use: it is carried
  on the Accord obligation binding (`AccordObligationExtensionInfo.canonicalAmount`),
  where the agreement layer knows the asset's decimals 鈥?deliberately *not* on the
  x402 wire fields, which stay atomic-unit strings + `asset` and carry no scale.

items.title: cli: make wallet x402 consume radius-sdk; delete the hand-rolled x402 client
items.body:
Stack: #1 鈫?#2 鈫?#6.

`radius-cli wallet x402` now uses `createRadiusFetch` from `radius-sdk/client`. The SDK parses the 402, picks the scheme, signs (Permit2 exact and upto, EIP-3009, x402 v1 and v2), retries, guards redirects and decodes the receipt. The CLI keeps the command surface and flags, keystore loading, prompts, JSON envelope, exit codes and stderr summary.

- Deleted `src/lib/x402/{protocol,handlers,permit2,eip3009}.ts` and their tests; `test/client-parity.test.ts` in the SDK covers them. `http.ts` moves to `src/lib/http.ts`. `chains.ts` replaced by the SDK's viem chains.
- The CLI still makes the first request itself, so a non-402 response never prompts for the keystore. The 402 is then replayed into the SDK through a custom `fetch`, so the server is not asked twice.
- Flags map to SDK hooks: threshold / prompt / no-TTY refusal in `onPaymentRequired` (policy in `src/lib/x402Policy.ts`, tested); `--x402-approve-permit2` / `-y` in `onApprovalRequired`.
- Gas sponsoring: when the server declares `eip2612GasSponsoring`, the SDK signs an EIP-2612 permit with the payment and no approval transaction is sent.
- New constraint: payments are in SBC only, on the configured network. The old code paid in whatever ERC-20 the server listed first, with the threshold read in that token's units. Non-SBC offers are now refused before signing. `--sbc` relocates the SBC contract; it does not select another asset. A multi-asset allowlist (`assets: [SBC, USDC]`, USD cap, `--asset`) is the follow-up.
- `radius-cli` now depends on `radius-sdk`, so the SDK must be published before the next CLI release.

Verified on testnet against `packages/sdk/examples/worker-seller` under `wrangler dev`: a fresh wallet holding only 0.005 SBC paid the $0.001 route with no approval transaction; Permit2 allowance 0 before and after; settlement tx `0xaeaf5bfdc891813823dee70a2b7270ab1a00f06bb408a75b2875cf677608f0a0`. items.title: @blueagent/x402 says v2-compatible but still uses legacy x402 HTTP fields
items.body:
Hi 鈥?I work on zFinia, an external x402 seller, and found this while checking whether our canonical Base-v2 endpoint could be used as an interoperability fixture.

`packages/x402-client/src/client.ts` currently describes `X402Client` as working with 鈥渁ny x402 v2 compatible endpoint鈥? but the request path still expects the older transport/data shape:

- reads `X-Payment-Requirements`
- reads `accepts[0].maxAmountRequired`
- retries with `X-Payment`
- reads `X-Payment-Response`

Canonical x402 v2 uses `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`, `accepts[].amount`, `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`, and `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`. A v2-only seller can therefore return a valid 402 and still fail before signing/retry in this client.

A narrow regression would be enough: mocked POST 鈫?402 containing a Base `eip155:8453` exact requirement with `amount` 鈫?signed retry using `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` 鈫?200 with `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`. If backward compatibility is intentional, version-gating modern vs legacy fields would avoid silently treating the legacy shape as v2.

Optional unpaid external fixture if useful:
- `POST https://api.zfinia.com/x402/v1/accessibility-contrast-calculator`
- discovery: `https://api.zfinia.com/.well-known/x402.json`
- deterministic body: `{"foreground":"#000000","background":"#ffffff","large_text":false}`
- Base exact-v2, 1000 atomic USDC ($0.001)

No funded test or purchase is requested; the mocked regression should be sufficient. If this is intentionally a legacy-compatible client despite the v2 wording, closing as such is totally fine.

## Reason

Keeper workflows cannot consume pay-per-call x402 APIs (the machine-economy standard where a server answers 402 with payment requirements, the client pays a few cents in USDC, and retries with an X-PAYMENT signature). KeeperHub itself sells workflow calls over x402 (`lib/payments/x402/`), but no workflow action can *buy* from an x402 endpoint.

Today the Webhook action hits a paid endpoint, gets 402, and surfaces an opaque `HTTP 402: ...` error. The workaround is hand-rolling fetch-then-402 logic in Code steps per workflow: no shared SSRF guard, no spend-cap discipline, duplicated everywhere. Evidence: `plugins/webhook/steps/send-webhook.ts` returns `HTTP ${status}` for any non-OK status with no 402 awareness.

Checked on staging @ `f8c8f18c7`; no x402 buyer exists in `plugins/` or `lib/` (only the seller-side gate).

## Scope

- New `x402` plugin with ONE action, `fetch-paid-resource`: GET/POST a URL via `safeFetch` + `assertUrlIsPublic` (same SSRF posture as webhook), parse x402 v1/v2 402 payment requirements, enforce a user-configured `maxPriceUsdc` spend cap, and retry with a caller-supplied `X-PAYMENT` value to return the paid data.
- Signing stays where it belongs: the signature comes from a template variable (agentic-wallet sign entrypoint / Code step), never from keys held by this node. No new key custody, no bypass of the A-06 fund-moving guard in `sign-typed-data`.
- Egress `user-destination` (plan-gated like webhook via the catch-all), unit tests in `tests/unit/`.
- NOT in scope: embedded wallet signing, new triggers, facilitator verify/settle (that is the resource server's job), protocol changes.

## Plan

Implement the plugin (`index.ts`, `icon.tsx`, `credentials.ts`, `test.ts`, `steps/fetch-paid-resource.ts`), register in `plugins/plugin-allowlist.json`, run `pnpm discover-plugins`, add unit tests, verify with `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm check`, and `pnpm test:unit`, then open a PR against `staging`.

Modern enterprise artificial intelligence has achieved unprecedented reasoning, planning, and natural language synthesis capabilities with foundation models such as Google Gemini 3.7. Whenever an autonomous software agent requires real-time, high-fidelity external intelligence鈥攔anging from localized ASEAN supply-chain freight costs and cold-chain compliance data to live foot-traffic footfall counts鈥攊t is blocked by traditional Web2 paywalls. In current commercial architectures, utilizing an external paid API requires a human operator to register an account, configure institutional credit cards, manage monthly recurring SaaS subscriptions, generate static API access tokens, and store sensitive secrets. Furthermore, traditional payment rails (such as credit cards or wire transfers) impose minimum transaction thresholds ($0.30+ fixed per-transaction fee on Stripe/Visa/Mastercard), rendering sub-cent or fractional-dollar **data micropayments mathematically and economically unfeasible**.

**NEXUS-GEMINI x402** resolves this fundamental paradigm limitation by establishing an end-to-end, multi-agent autonomous commerce and intelligence architecture. The inspiration for NEXUS-GEMINI x402 stems from two convergent tectonic shifts in technology:

## 2. Mathematical Formulations & Economic Governance Models

### 2.1 The Agentic Business Value (ABV) Equation
The platform quantifies the aggregate business value delivered by an autonomous multi-agent execution run via the multiplicative **ABV Index**:

$$\text{ABV} = I \times E \times C \times T$$

Where:
- **$I \in [0, 10]$ (Intelligence Quality)**: Evaluates the Gemini Commander's reasoning depth, semantic decomposition fidelity, and multi-source synthesis coherence.
- **$E \in [0, 10]$ (Execution Success)**: Measures the ratio of successfully discovered, negotiated, and completed HTTP 402 data handshakes without retry exhaustion.
- **$C \in [0, 10]$ (Economic Efficiency)**: Evaluates the Expected Value ($\text{EV}$) unlocked per unit of USDC spent from the agent treasury:
  $$C = \min\left(10, \frac{\sum \text{EV}_{\text{unlocked}}}{\sum \text{Cost}_{\text{settled}}} \times \alpha\right)$$
- **$T \in [0, 10]$ (Trust & Governance Compliance)**: Measures absolute adherence to human budget constraints ($B_{\max}$), verifiable zero-leakage cryptographic proof, and absence of hallucinated facts.

$$\text{Scale Range: } 0 \le \text{ABV} \le 10{,}000$$

### 2.2 The Strategic Intelligence Value (SIV) Index
To assess cross-functional strategic balance across intelligence domains, the SIV metric calculates the geometric product of six normalized domain parameters:

$$\text{SIV} = \left( R \times A \times C \times E \times G \times L \right) \times 100$$

Where:

- **$A \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Analysis Rigor)**: Statistical confidence and econometric modeling.

- **$L \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (System Learning & Cache Hit Rate)**: Reusability of acquired verified data.

$$\mathbb{E}[\text{Value}] > \kappa \cdot \text{Cost}_{\text{USDC}} \quad \text{subject to} \quad \sum_{i=1}^{k} \text{Cost}_i \le B_{\max}$$

2. **`NEXUS-02-DSC` (Discovery Agent)**: Probes distributed HTTP 402 endpoints across Southeast Asia, querying metadata headers (`X-402-Price`, `X-402-Recipient`, `X-402-Network`, and quality scores) to construct candidate purchase vectors.
3. **`NEXUS-03-STR` (Strategy Agent)**: Evaluates ROI, expected value vs micro-cost ratios, and cross-checks with historical cache to avoid redundant expenditure.
4. **`NEXUS-04-SOL` (Commerce Agent)**: Executes the programmatic HTTP 402 handshake:

   - Encapsulates Solana keypair in devnet sandboxed vault

   - Awaits sub-second slot confirmation
   - Retries request with `X-Payment-Signature: <base58_signature>` $\rightarrow$ Receives `200 OK`
5. **`NEXUS-05-VRF` (Verification Agent)**: Validates cryptographic signature uniqueness, recipient address matching, and generates immutable forensic audit proofs.

---

## 4. How the Platform Works: Step-by-Step Execution Sequence

1. **User Objective Formulation**: A business executive or analyst inputs a natural language mission (e.g., *"Evaluate Johor Bahru vs Penang for semiconductor logistics expansion under $2.00 USDC"*).
2. **Commander Initialization**: The Commander defines variables: Freight Index, Port Throughput, Cross-Border FX, and Labour Cost.
3. **Autonomous Discovery**: The Discovery Agent identifies two relevant data endpoints (`oracle-penang-freight` at $0.15 USDC and `oracle-cross-border-fx` at $0.05 USDC).
4. **Hurdle Verification**: Strategy Agent calculates total cost ($0.20 USDC) versus expected strategic decision value ($4.80 USDC) = 24.0x ROI ratio, well above the $\kappa = 1.5$ threshold.
5. **Micropayment Handshake**: The Commerce Agent pays the oracles via Solana Devnet with ~0.000005 SOL fee and 420ms finality.
6. **Data Injection & Synthesis**: Unlocked raw datasets are fed back into Gemini 3.7 Flash.
7. **Deliverable Production**: The UI immediately renders an interactive, multi-dimensional Strategic Report, featuring Executive Synthesis, Market Opportunities, Financial Feasibility Model, Risk Assessment & Mitigation Matrix, 3-Phase Action Plan, and on-chain Solscan receipts.

| Layer | Technologies Used | Purpose |
|---|---|---|

| **Blockchain Settlement** | Solana Devnet & SPL Token Standard | Sub-second micro-settlement, non-custodial agent vaults, immutable audit ledger |
| **Protocol Specification**| RFC HTTP 402 Payment Required Handshake | Universal web standard for programmatic machine-to-machine value exchange |
| **Backend Runtime** | Node.js, Express, TypeScript, `esbuild` | Server-side secure routing, API proxying, and key encapsulation |
| **Frontend UI** | React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4 | High-Density tactical terminal layout, responsive telemetry pipelines, canvas-confetti |
| **Icons & Viz** | Lucide React, SVG Micro-charts | Visual telemetry, pulsing status indicators, and cryptographic receipts |

---

## 6. Challenges Faced & Solutions

1. **Challenge: Preventing Agent Spending Runaway**
   - *Solution*: Implemented a strict two-tier governance architecture: a hard-coded $B_{\max}$ lifetime cap in the server-side treasury vault and an auto-approve transaction threshold ($2.00 USDC).
2. **Challenge: Achieving True HTTP 402 Compliance**
   - *Solution*: Developed a RFC-compliant Express middleware that returns genuine `HTTP 402` status codes with `WWW-Authenticate: x402-solana-v1` and custom headers, verifying base58 Solana transaction signatures before unblocking data.
3. **Challenge: Eliminating Context Window Bloat**
   - *Solution*: Utilized specialized agent handoffs where intermediate agents only pass structured schemas and economic authorizations rather than raw LLM conversational history.

---

## 7. What We Learned

- **Micro-economies unlock real intelligence**: When AI agents can spend fractional cents on-demand, data providers are incentivized to expose high-value proprietary feeds without subscription lock-in.
- **Solana is the ideal settlement layer for agentic commerce**: Sub-second block times (400ms) match LLM reasoning speeds, and $0.00025 transaction costs make $0.05 micro-queries viable.
- **Human-in-the-loop governance builds enterprise trust**: Transparent visual telemetry, budget ceiling bounds, and on-chain cryptographic receipts provide the forensic auditability required for enterprise adoption.

---

## 8. Future Scalability & Commercial Roadmap

1. **Multi-Chain x402 Gateways**: Expanding from Solana to cross-chain liquidity pools via Wormhole and Circle CCTP.
2. **Decentralized Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Bidding Marketplaces**: Enabling autonomous AI agents to contract and pay sub-agents for specialized micro-tasks (e.g. Monte Carlo simulations, geospatial analysis).
3. **Cross-Border DuitNow / QRIS On-Ramps**: Direct fiat-to-Solana micropayment bridging for Malaysian and ASEAN SMEs.
4. **Enterprise Multi-Sig Vaults**: Integration with Squads Protocol on Solana for corporate multi-stakeholder governance over agent fleets.

## Summary

Adds a self-contained x402 example demonstrating how a developer can pay for a protected resource using a Swig wallet.

## What changed

- Added reusable setup that validates or provisions:
  - Facilitator, developer, and resource-provider identities
  - Swig wallet
  - SPL token mint
  - Source and destination token accounts
  - Required SOL and token balances
- Added a local x402 facilitator with Swig smart-wallet verification.
- Added an x402-protected weather resource server.
- Added a developer flow that:
  - Receives the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` challenge
  - Prepares the payment with `wallet.x402.prepareFromResponse()`
  - Signs the prepared transaction
  - Constructs the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header
  - Retries and receives the protected resource
- Added configuration and usage documentation.
- Updated the workspace lockfile with the example dependencies.

Generated setup state is cached in the gitignored `.local/state.json`. Identity keypairs may be supplied through environment variables or generated during setup.

## Validation

- Example TypeScript typecheck passes.
- Prettier and `git diff --check` pass.
- Complete setup, preparation, signing, facilitator verification, settlement, and paid-resource flow tested successfully against Surfpool.
